newsitem.title: USA: US rail freight traffic down from year ago--AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail freight traffic down from year ago--AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail freight traffic in the week ended November 30, because of the Thanksgiving Day holiday, fell sharply from the year-ago week, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.

AAR reported 295,434 carloads last week, down 18.5 percent from 362,540 in the year-ago week, which did not include a holiday. It said intermodal traffic, which does not include carloads, totaled 136,556 trailers and containers in the week, a 12.8 percent decline from 156,600 in the year-ago week.
Ton-miles decreased 18.6 percent to 21.9 billion from 26.9 billion a year ago. A ton-mile, a measure of freight transportation, equals one ton of freight hauled one mile.
But Harvey Levine, AAR chief economist, noted that "no meaningful comparisons can be drawn because we are comparing a holiday week this year with a non-holiday week last year."

All commodity groups reported by AAR had declines in carloads from a year ago. Grain loadings fell 29.5 percent to 21,129 carloads in the November 30 week from 29,969 a year ago, and farm products other than grain were down 26.5 percent to 1,713 carloads from 2,332 a year ago.
AAR said carloads of metallic ores fell 12.9 percent to 17,611 in the week from 20,215 in the year-ago week.
Lumber and wood products decreased 23 percent to 4,094 carloads from 5,314, AAR said.
Petroleum loadings, at 4,372 in the week, were off 22.2 percent from 5,618 last year. AAR also said that carloads of coal decreased 12 percent to 119,106 from 135,346 a year ago.
Motor vehicles and equipment fell 27.6 percent to 15,174 carloads from 20,946 in the same 1995 week.
Grain mill products were off 5.5 percent to 8,927 carloads in the week from 9,444 in the year-ago week, AAR said.
In the first 48 weeks of 1996, AAR said ton-miles rose 1.9 percent from the same period last year. Intermodal traffic also rose 1.9 percent, but carloads fell 0.6 percent, AAR said.
